I will mostly do what has kept my family steady here: keep most land in wheat-maize, and leave a smaller piece for cotton. On 33 mu, I will put 25 mu into the wheat-maize land and 8 mu into cotton. That way I do not spread myself too thin with only 2 people in the house. I have farmed a long time, and when I am not sure, I look at what works in nearby fields with well water. Wheat and maize are the main food and cash together, so I will not cut fertilizer too hard there. Losing yield hurts more than wasting a little fertilizer. On wheat land, I will use enough base fertilizer and then topdress once when the crop starts pulling hard; with irrigation from the well, I can push for a steady stand. After wheat, I will hurry in maize on the same 25 mu and feed it a bit heavier on nitrogen, because maize eats strong in summer. Cotton I will keep on 8 mu only, because it needs more watching and more spraying. I will not gamble on fancy new ways. I will use the kinds and amounts I have seen work around me, give water when the crop really needs it, and spend more on the wheat-maize side because that land carries the year.
